This year, I got my hands on some apples fresh from the tree, and wanted to do something I've been wanting to do for years: Brew my own apple cider.

I didn't know how well it'd turn out, so I didn't want to spend all sorts of money and time on top end equipment, but it didn't look like I'd need to.

I picked up a juicer to begin with, and started juicing the apples. Once I had a large pot of juice, I heated it to 80C for about a minute to kill anything in the juice.

At the same time, I was using some sterilizing solution on all the things I'd be working with: the airlocks, the tube, and the jugs.

Once the juice had cooled, I siphoned it into a pair of 4l jugs using some clear flexible tube I picked up at the hardware store.

Once I was confident the juice had cooled below 40C, I pitched some champagne yeast into both jugs and attached the airlocks.

I made a mistake at this point. I left it for a week, and assumed it was ready (because reading is for squares, man!), and bottled it by siphoning it using my clear plastic tube (and avoiding the crud on the bottom of the jug). Taking a few sips, I quickly realized there's no way that cider was ready (cider isn't supposed to taste like a bakery...), so I sent it back to the (newly cleaned and sanitized) jugs.

about 3 weeks later, I bottled it again, and it turned out much better. I've given a few people some samples of the finished product, and the general consensus is that it's not bad for a first try.

I've kept about 4l for later. I've read pretty consistently that it gets better with age.

Pretty minor time commitment, and the end result can get you drunk? I think I have a new hobby.
